modelEssay.title: The Importance of Having a Sense of Family Responsibility
modelEssay.content:
In contemporary society, the significance of possessing a sense of family responsibility cannot be overstated. It is the cornerstone that upholds the stability and harmony of a family. Firstly, a sense of responsibility fosters mutual respect and care, which are essential for maintaining strong family bonds. When family members take on their roles and duties, they contribute to a nurturing environment where love and support thrive.

Moreover, a strong sense of family responsibility is crucial for the upbringing of children. It instills in them the values of commitment and reliability, shaping them into responsible adults who are capable of contributing positively to society. Children who grow up in families where responsibility is valued are more likely to develop a strong moral compass and a sense of empathy towards others.

In conclusion, having a sense of family responsibility is indispensable. It not only strengthens familial ties but also shapes the character of future generations. As society evolves, the importance of this value remains constant, reminding us of our inherent duties towards our loved ones.

transcript.text: Excuse me, where's your rock music section?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 打扰一下，你们的摇滚乐专区在哪儿？

transcript.text: Rock music? I'm sorry, we're a jazz store. We don't have any rock and roll.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 摇滚乐？抱歉，我们是一家爵士乐唱片店，不卖摇滚乐。

transcript.text: Oh, you only have jazz music? Nothing else?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 哦，你们只有爵士乐吗？别的都没有？

transcript.text: That's right. We're the only record store in London dedicated exclusively to jazz.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 是的。我们是伦敦唯一一家专营爵士乐的唱片店。

transcript.text: Actually, we're more than just a record store. We have a cafe and library upstairs,
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 其实我们不只是唱片店。楼上有咖啡馆和图书室，

transcript.text: and a ticket office down the hall where you can buy tickets to all the major jazz concerts in the city.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 走廊尽头还有售票处，在那儿可以买到全城所有大型爵士音乐会的门票。

transcript.text: Also, we have our own studio next door where we produce albums for up-and-coming artists.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 隔壁还有我们自己的录音棚，为崭露头角的艺人制作专辑。

transcript.text: We're committed to fostering new music talent.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我们致力于培养新的音乐人才。

transcript.text: Wow, that's so cool. I guess there's not much of a jazz scene anymore, not like there used to be.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 哇，太棒了。我想如今爵士乐的圈子已经不像从前那样热闹了。

transcript.text: But here you're trying to promote this great music genre.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 而你们在这里努力推广这一伟大的音乐流派。

transcript.text: Yes, indeed. Nowadays, most people like to listen to pop and rock music.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 确实如此。如今大多数人喜欢听流行乐和摇滚乐。

transcript.text: Hip-hop music from America is also getting more and more popular.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 来自美国的嘻哈音乐也越来越受欢迎。

transcript.text: So as a result, there are fewer listeners of jazz, which is a great shame, because it's an incredibly rich genre.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 结果爵士乐的听众越来越少，这很可惜，因为它是一个极其丰富的流派。

transcript.text: But that's not to say there isn't any good new jazz music being made out there anymore. Far from it.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但这并不是说如今就没有出色的新爵士乐了，远非如此。

transcript.text: It's just a much smaller market today.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 只是今天的市场小得多了。

transcript.text: So how would you define jazz?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 那你会怎样定义爵士乐呢？

transcript.text: Well, interestingly enough, there's no agreed-upon definition of jazz.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 有意思的是，爵士乐并没有一个公认的定义。

transcript.text: Indeed, there are many different styles of jazz. Some have singing, but most don't.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 爵士乐确实有很多不同的风格。有些有演唱，但大多数没有。

transcript.text: Some are electric and some aren't. Some contain live experimentation, but not always.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 有些是电声的，有些不是。有些包含现场即兴试验，但并非总是如此。

transcript.text: While there's no simple definition for it, and while there are many different styles of jazz, you simply know it when you hear it.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 虽然它没有简单的定义，风格也多种多样，但你一听就知道那是爵士乐。

transcript.text: Honestly, the only way to know what jazz is, is listen to it yourself.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 老实说，要知道什么是爵士乐，唯一的办法就是自己去听。

transcript.text: As the great trumpet player Louis Armstrong said,
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 正如伟大的小号手路易斯·阿姆斯特朗所说，

transcript.text: If you gotta ask, you'll never know.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 如果你还得问，那你永远不会懂。

transcript.text: There's a lot about Leo Sanchez and his farm in Salinas, California that seems unusual.
transcript.translation: 利奥·桑切斯和他在加利福尼亚州萨利纳斯的农场有许多地方显得与众不同。

transcript.text: The national average farm size is around 440 acres, but his is only one acre.
transcript.translation: 全国农场的平均规模约为440英亩，而他的农场只有1英亩。

transcript.text: The average age of farmers hovers around 58 years old, but he is just 26.
transcript.translation: 农场主的平均年龄在58岁左右，而他只有26岁。

transcript.text: And Sanchez constantly attempts to improve everything from seeding techniques out in the field to the promotion and sale of his produce online.
transcript.translation: 桑切斯还不断改进各个环节，从田间的播种技术到农产品的网上推广和销售。

transcript.text: This is evidence of an experimental approach.
transcript.translation: 这体现出一种勇于试验的做法。

transcript.text: It's an approach not dictated by the confines of conventional, large-scale agriculture led by international corporations.
transcript.translation: 这种做法不受由跨国公司主导的传统大规模农业的条条框框所限制。

transcript.text: While farming is often difficult for both the body and mind, Sanchez says he and many of his fellow young farmers are motivated by a desire to set a new standard for agriculture.
transcript.translation: 尽管务农往往对身心都是挑战，桑切斯说，他和许多年轻同行的动力来自为农业树立新标准的愿望。

transcript.text: Many of them are employing a multitude of technologies, some new and some not so new.
transcript.translation: 他们中的许多人都在使用多种技术，有些是新技术，有些则不那么新。

transcript.text: Recently, Sanchez bought a hand-operated tool which pulls out weeds and loosens soil.
transcript.translation: 最近，桑切斯买了一件手动工具，既能拔草又能松土。

transcript.text: It actually dates back to at least 1701.
transcript.translation: 这种工具的历史其实至少可以追溯到1701年。

transcript.text: It stands in sharp contrast to Sanchez's other gadget, a gas-powered flame weed killer invented in 1997.
transcript.translation: 它与桑切斯的另一件装备形成鲜明对比——那是一台1997年发明的燃气火焰除草机。

transcript.text: He simply doesn't discriminate when it comes to the newness of tools. If it works, it works.
transcript.translation: 在工具的新旧上他并不挑剔。管用就行。

transcript.text: Farmers have a long history of invention and it's no different today.
transcript.translation: 农场主历来善于发明创造，今天依然如此。

transcript.text: Young farmers are guided by their love for agriculture and aided by their knowledge of technology.
transcript.translation: 年轻的农场主们凭着对农业的热爱，借助自己的技术知识。

transcript.text: To find inexpensive and appropriately sized tools, they collaborate and innovate.
transcript.translation: 为了找到价格低廉、大小合适的工具，他们相互协作、不断创新。

transcript.text: Sometimes the old stuff just works better or more efficiently.
transcript.translation: 有时候，老东西反而更好用、更高效。

transcript.text: Eat Grub is Britain's first new food company that breaks Western food boundaries by introducing edible insects as a new source of food.
transcript.translation: Eat Grub 是英国第一家打破西方饮食界限、把可食用昆虫引入作为新食物来源的新型食品公司。

transcript.text: And Sainsbury's is the first UK supermarket to stock the company's crunchy roasted crickets.
transcript.translation: 而 Sainsbury's 是英国第一家上架该公司香脆烤蟋蟀的超市。

transcript.text: Sainsbury's insists that such food is no joke and could be a new sustainable source of protein.
transcript.translation: Sainsbury's 坚称这类食品并非玩笑，可能成为一种新的可持续蛋白质来源。

transcript.text: Out of curiosity, I paid a visit to Sainsbury's.
transcript.translation: 出于好奇，我去了一趟 Sainsbury's。

transcript.text: As I put my hand into a packet of crickets with their tiny eyes and legs, the idea of one going in my mouth made me feel a little sick.
transcript.translation: 当我把手伸进一包长着细小眼睛和腿的蟋蟀里时，想到要把其中一只放进嘴里，就有点反胃。

transcript.text: But the first bite was a pleasant surprise.
transcript.translation: 但第一口却是个惊喜。

transcript.text: A little dry and lacking in taste, but at least a wing didn't get stuck in my throat.
transcript.translation: 有点干，也没什么味道，但至少没有翅膀卡在喉咙里。

transcript.text: The roasted seasoning largely overpowered any other flavour, although there was a slightly bitter aftertaste.
transcript.translation: 烘烤的调味料几乎盖过了其他味道，不过留下一点苦涩的回味。

transcript.text: The texture was crunchy, but smelt a little of cat food.
transcript.translation: 口感是脆的，但闻起来有点像猫粮。

transcript.text: Eat Grub also recommends the crickets as a topping for noodles, soups and salads.
transcript.translation: Eat Grub 还建议把蟋蟀撒在面条、汤和沙拉上做配料。

transcript.text: The company boasts that its dried crickets contain more protein than beef, chicken and pork, as well as minerals like iron and calcium.
transcript.translation: 该公司宣称，其干蟋蟀所含的蛋白质高于牛肉、鸡肉和猪肉，还富含铁、钙等矿物质。

transcript.text: Unlike the production of meat, bugs do not use up large amounts of land, water or feed, and insect farming also produces far fewer greenhouse gases.
transcript.translation: 与肉类生产不同，昆虫不会消耗大量土地、水或饲料，昆虫养殖产生的温室气体也少得多。

transcript.text: However, despite 2 billion people worldwide already supplementing their diet with insects, consumer disgust remains a large barrier in many western countries.
transcript.translation: 然而，尽管全球已有20亿人把昆虫作为膳食补充，消费者的厌恶感在许多西方国家仍是一大障碍。

transcript.text: I'm not sure bugs will become a popular snack any time soon, but they're definitely food for thought.
transcript.translation: 我不确定虫子短期内会成为流行零食，但它们确实值得深思。

transcript.text: Recording 1.
transcript.translation: 录音一。

transcript.text: Have you ever had someone try to explain something to you a dozen times with no luck?
transcript.translation: 你是否有过这样的经历：别人给你讲了十几遍某件事，你还是没听懂？

transcript.text: But then when you see a picture, the idea finally clicks.
transcript.translation: 可当你看到一张图，那个概念一下子就明白了。

transcript.text: If that sounds familiar, maybe you might consider yourself a visual learner.
transcript.translation: 如果这听起来很耳熟，也许你会认为自己是视觉型学习者。

transcript.text: Or if reading or listening does the trick, maybe you feel like you're a verbal learner.
transcript.translation: 或者，如果阅读或聆听对你更管用，你可能觉得自己是言语型学习者。

transcript.text: We call these labels learning styles.
transcript.translation: 我们把这些标签称作学习风格。

transcript.text: But is there really a way to categorize different types of students?
transcript.translation: 但真的存在一种给不同类型的学生分类的方法吗？

transcript.text: Well, it actually seems that multiple presentation formats, especially if one of them is visual, help most people learn.
transcript.translation: 实际上，多种呈现方式——尤其是其中一种为视觉形式——似乎对大多数人的学习都有帮助。

transcript.text: When psychologists and educators test for learning styles,
transcript.translation: 心理学家和教育工作者测试学习风格时，

transcript.text: they're trying to figure out whether these are inherent traits that affect how well students learn, instead of just a preference.
transcript.translation: 他们想弄清楚的是：这些究竟是影响学生学习效果的固有特质，还是仅仅是一种偏好。

transcript.text: Usually, they start by giving a survey to figure out what style a student favours, like visual or verbal learning.
transcript.translation: 通常，他们先做一份问卷，找出学生偏爱哪种风格，比如视觉型还是言语型。

transcript.text: Then, they try to teach the students something with a specific presentation style, like using visual aids,
transcript.translation: 然后，他们用某种特定的呈现方式给学生讲授内容，比如使用视觉辅助材料，

transcript.text: and do a follow-up test to see how much they learned.
transcript.translation: 再做一次后续测试，看学生掌握了多少。

transcript.text: That way, the researchers can see if the self-identified verbal learners really learned better when the information was just spoken aloud, for example.
transcript.translation: 这样一来，研究者就能看出，比如自认的言语型学习者，是否在信息只以口头方式传达时学得更好。

transcript.text: But, according to a 2008 review, only one study that followed this design found that students actually learned best with their preferred style.
transcript.translation: 但根据2008年的一篇综述，采用这种设计的研究中，只有一项发现学生用自己偏好的方式确实学得最好。

transcript.text: But the study had some big flaws.
transcript.translation: 然而这项研究存在一些重大缺陷。

transcript.text: The researchers excluded two-thirds of the original participants because they didn't seem to have any clear learning style from the survey at the beginning.
transcript.translation: 研究者剔除了最初三分之二的受试者，因为他们在开始的问卷中没有表现出明确的学习风格。

transcript.text: And they didn't even report the actual test scores in the final paper.
transcript.translation: 而且他们在最终的论文里甚至没有报告实际的测试分数。

transcript.text: So, it doesn't really seem like learning styles are an inherent trait that we all have.
transcript.translation: 所以，学习风格似乎并不是我们人人都有的固有特质。

transcript.text: But that doesn't mean that all students will do amazingly if they just spend all their time reading from a textbook.
transcript.translation: 但这并不意味着，学生只要把全部时间用来读课本就能学得很好。

transcript.text: Instead, most people seem to learn better if they're taught in several ways, especially if one is visual.
transcript.translation: 相反，多数人在以多种方式受教时似乎学得更好，尤其是其中一种为视觉形式时。

transcript.text: In one study, researchers tested whether students remembered lists of words better if they heard them, saw them, or both.
transcript.translation: 在一项研究中，研究者测试了学生记忆单词表的效果：听、看，还是二者兼有。

transcript.text: And everyone seemed to do better if they got to see the words in print.
transcript.translation: 结果所有人在能看到印刷出来的单词时表现都更好。

transcript.text: Even the self-identified auditory learners. Their preference didn't seem to matter.
transcript.translation: 连自认的听觉型学习者也是如此。他们的偏好似乎并不重要。

transcript.text: Similar studies tested whether students learned basic physics and chemistry concepts better by reading plain text or viewing pictures, too.
transcript.translation: 类似的研究还测试了学生学习基础物理和化学概念时，读纯文本和看图哪种效果更好。

transcript.text: And everyone did better with the help of pictures.
transcript.translation: 结果所有人在有图片帮助时都表现更好。

transcript.text: Free market capitalism hasn't freed us. It has trapped us.
transcript.translation: 自由市场资本主义并没有让我们获得自由，反而把我们困住了。

transcript.text: It's imperative for us to embrace a workplace revolution.
transcript.translation: 我们必须迎来一场职场变革。

transcript.text: We are unlikely to spend our last moments regretting that we didn't spend enough of our lives slaving away at work.
transcript.translation: 在生命的最后时刻，我们不太可能后悔没有把更多的人生耗在没日没夜的工作上。

transcript.text: We may instead find ourselves feeling guilty about the time we didn't spend watching our children grow, or with our loved ones, or traveling, or on the cultural or leisure pursuits that bring us happiness.
transcript.translation: 相反，我们可能会因为没有时间陪伴孩子成长、没有时间和亲人相处、没有时间旅行、没有时间从事那些带来快乐的文化娱乐活动而感到内疚。

transcript.text: Unfortunately, the average full-time employee in the world works 42 hours a week, well over a third of the time we're awake.
transcript.translation: 遗憾的是，全球全职员工平均每周工作42小时，远超我们清醒时间的三分之一。

transcript.text: Some of our all-too-precious time is being stolen.
transcript.translation: 我们无比宝贵的时间正在被偷走。

transcript.text: Office workers do around 2 billion hours of unpaid overtime each year.
transcript.translation: 上班族每年无偿加班约20亿小时。

transcript.text: So it's extremely welcome that some government coalitions have started looking into potentially cutting the working week to four days.
transcript.translation: 因此，一些政府联盟已开始研究把每周工作日缩短至四天的可能性，这非常值得欢迎。

transcript.text: The champions of free market capitalism promised their way of life would bring us freedom, but it wasn't freedom at all.
transcript.translation: 自由市场资本主义的拥护者曾承诺，他们的生活方式会带来自由，但那根本不是自由。

transcript.text: From the lack of secure affordable housing to growing job insecurity and rising personal debt, the individual is trapped.
transcript.translation: 从缺乏稳定且负担得起的住房，到日益加剧的就业不稳定和不断上升的个人债务，个体被困住了。

transcript.text: Nine decades ago, leading economists predicted that technological advances and rising productivity would mean that we'd be working a 15-hour week by now.
transcript.translation: 九十年前，顶尖经济学家曾预言，技术进步和生产率提高意味着我们如今每周只需工作15小时。

transcript.text: That target has been somewhat missed.
transcript.translation: 这个目标显然落空了。

transcript.text: Here is the most malignant threat to our personal freedom, particularly as the balance of power in the workplace has been shifted so dramatically from worker to boss.
transcript.translation: 这正是对我们个人自由最恶劣的威胁，尤其是职场权力格局已如此剧烈地从劳动者一方转向老板一方。

transcript.text: A huge portion of our lives involves the surrender of our freedom and personal autonomy.
transcript.translation: 我们生命中很大一部分都意味着交出自由和个人自主权。

transcript.text: It's time in which we are directed by the needs and desires of others and denied the right to make our own choices.
transcript.translation: 在这段时间里，我们被他人的需求和愿望所支配，被剥夺了自己作选择的权利。

transcript.text: That's bad for us.
transcript.translation: 这对我们有害。

transcript.text: It's hardly surprising that over half a million workers suffer from work-related mental health conditions each year.
transcript.translation: 因此毫不奇怪，每年有五十多万劳动者患上与工作相关的心理健康疾病。

transcript.text: All told, 15.4 million working days were lost to work-related stress last year, a jump of nearly a quarter.
transcript.translation: 总计有1540万个工作日因与工作相关的压力而损失，比前一年增加了近四分之一。

transcript.text: Yes, there are those who, far from being overworked, actually seek more hours.
transcript.translation: 确实，也有一些人远谈不上工作过度，反而想要更多工时。

transcript.text: But a shorter working week would enable us to redistribute hours from the overworked to the underworked.
transcript.translation: 但缩短每周工时能让我们把工时从工作过度者那里重新分配给工作不足者。

transcript.text: We need to look at ways of cutting the working week without slashing living standards.
transcript.translation: 我们需要研究在不压低生活水平的前提下缩短工时的办法。

transcript.text: After all, the world's workers have already suffered the worst deduction in wages since the early 1800s.
transcript.translation: 毕竟，全球劳动者已经经历了自19世纪初以来最严重的工资缩水。

transcript.text: And cutting the working week would be conducive to the individual, giving millions of workers more time to spend as they see fit.
transcript.translation: 而缩短每周工时对个人有益，能让数百万劳动者有更多可以自行支配的时间。

transcript.text: Today I'm going to talk about Germany's dream airport in Berlin.
transcript.translation: 今天我要讲的是德国柏林的那座梦想机场。

transcript.text: The airport looks exactly like every other major modern airport in Europe, except for one big problem.
transcript.translation: 这座机场看上去和欧洲其他任何一座现代化大型机场别无二致，只有一个大问题。

transcript.text: More than seven years after it was originally supposed to open, it still stands empty.
transcript.translation: 在原定开放日期过去七年多之后，它依然空无一人。

transcript.text: Germany is known for its efficiency and refined engineering, but when it comes to its new ghost airport, this reputation could not be further from the truth.
transcript.translation: 德国以效率和精湛的工程技术闻名，但说到这座新的“幽灵机场”，这一声誉与事实相去甚远。

transcript.text: Plagued by long delays, perpetual mismanagement, and ever-soaring costs, the airport has become something of a joke among Germans, and a source of frustration for local politicians, business leaders, and residents alike.
transcript.translation: 长期延误、管理持续混乱、成本不断飙升，使这座机场成了德国人眼中的笑柄，也让当地政界人士、企业领袖和居民倍感沮丧。

transcript.text: Planning for the new airport began in 1989.
transcript.translation: 新机场的规划始于1989年。

transcript.text: At the time, it became clear that the newly reunified Berlin would need a modern airport with far greater capacity than its existing airports.
transcript.translation: 当时人们清楚地意识到，刚刚重新统一的柏林需要一座容量远超现有机场的现代化机场。

transcript.text: The city broke ground on the new airport in 2006.
transcript.translation: 该市于2006年为新机场破土动工。

transcript.text: The first major sign of problems came in summer 2010, when the Construction Corporation pushed the opening from October 2011 to June 2012.
transcript.translation: 问题的第一个重大信号出现在2010年夏天，当时施工公司把开放时间从2011年10月推迟到2012年6月。

transcript.text: In 2012, the city planned an opening ceremony, but less than a month beforehand, inspectors found significant problems with the fire safety system and pushed the opening back again to 2013.
transcript.translation: 2012年，该市原本安排了开放典礼，但不到一个月前，检查人员发现消防系统存在严重问题，开放时间又被推迟到2013年。

transcript.text: It wasn't just the smoke system. Many other major problems subsequently emerged.
transcript.translation: 问题不只出在排烟系统上。随后又冒出许多其他重大问题。

transcript.text: More than 90 kilometres of cable were incorrectly installed.
transcript.translation: 有90多公里的电缆铺设有误。

transcript.text: Four thousand doors were wrongly numbered. Escalators were too short, and there was a shortage of check-in desks.
transcript.translation: 四千扇门编号错误，自动扶梯太短，值机柜台也不够。

transcript.text: So why, with so many problems discovered, didn't the Airport Corporation decide to give up on the project and start over?
transcript.translation: 那么，既然发现了这么多问题，机场公司为什么不干脆放弃项目、重新来过呢？

transcript.text: The reason is simple. People are often hesitant to terminate a project when they've already invested time or resources into it, even if it might make logical sense to do so.
transcript.translation: 原因很简单。人们在已经投入时间或资源之后，往往不愿终止一个项目，哪怕从逻辑上看终止才是合理的。

transcript.text: The longer the delays continued, the more problems inspectors found.
transcript.translation: 延期拖得越久，检查人员发现的问题就越多。

transcript.text: Leadership of the Planning Corporation has changed hands nearly as many times as the opening date has been pushed back.
transcript.translation: 规划公司的管理层更换的次数，几乎和开放日期推迟的次数一样多。

transcript.text: Initially, rather than appointing a general contractor to run the project, the Corporation decided to manage it themselves, despite lack of experience with an undertaking of that scale.
transcript.translation: 起初，公司没有聘请总承包商来管理项目，而是决定自己管理，尽管缺乏操作这种规模工程的经验。

transcript.text: To compound the delays, the unused airport is resulting in massive costs.
transcript.translation: 更糟的是，这座闲置的机场还带来了巨额开支。

transcript.text: Every month it remains unopened costs between 9 and 10 million euros.
transcript.translation: 机场每空置一个月，就要花费900万至1000万欧元。

transcript.text: Assuming all goes well, the airport should open in October 2020.
transcript.translation: 如果一切顺利，机场应在2020年10月开放。

transcript.text: But the still empty airport stands as the biggest embarrassment to Germany's reputation for efficiency and a continuing drain on city and state resources.
transcript.translation: 但这座仍然空荡荡的机场，成了德国效率声誉最大的难堪，也在持续消耗着市和州的财政资源。

paragraphs.text: The number of devices you can talk to is multiplying—first it was your phone, then your car, and now you can tell your kitchen appliance what to do. But even without gadgets that understand our spoken commands, research suggests that, as bizarre as it sounds, under certain __26__, people regularly ascribe human traits to everyday objects.

paragraphs.text: Sometimes we see things as human because we are __27__. In one experiment, people who reported feeling isolated were more likely than others to attribute __28__ to various gadgets. In turn, feeling close to objects can __29__ loneliness. When college students were reminded of a time when they had been __30__ in a social setting they compensated by exaggerating their number of friends—unless they were first given tasks that caused them to interact with their phone as if it had human qualities. The phone __31__ stood in for real friends.

Further, the more their computer gave them problems, the more likely the respondents were to report that it had its own "beliefs and __32__".
paragraphs.translation: 在其他时候，我们为了理解产品而将其拟人化。一项研究发现，四分之三的受访者会对他们的电脑大喊大叫。此外，他们的电脑给他们带来的问题越多，受访者就越有可能报告说它有自己的'信念和欲望'。

paragraphs.translation: 那么人们如何将特质分配给物体呢？部分上，我们依赖外表。在人类身上，宽脸与支配性相关联。类似地，人们将宽脸的汽车、钟表和手表评价为比窄脸的更具支配性外观，并更喜欢它们——尤其是在竞争性场合。对德国汽车销售的分析发现，像微笑一样向上翘起的护栅汽车卖得最好。购买者将这一特征视为增加了汽车的友好性。

material.title: How Much Protein Do You Really Need?

paragraphs.text: The marketing is enticing: Get stronger muscles and healthier bodies with minimal effort by adding protein powder to your morning shake or juice drink. Or grab a protein bar at lunch or for a quick snack. Today, you can find protein supplements everywhere-online, at the pharmacy, grocery store, or health food store. They come in powders, pills, and bars. With more than $12 billion in sales this year, the industry is booming and, according to the market research company, Grand View Research, is on track to sell billions more by 2025. But do we really need all this supplemental protein? It depends. There are pros, cons and some ho-hums to consider.
paragraphs.translation: 营销宣传很诱人：通过在早餐奶昔或果汁饮料中加入蛋白粉，可以轻松获得更强壮的肌肉和更健康的身体。或者午餐时吃个蛋白棒作为快速零食。如今，蛋白补充剂无处不在——网上、药房、杂货店或健康食品店。它们有粉末、药片和棒状等形式。今年销售额超过120亿美元，这个行业正蓬勃发展，根据市场研究公司Grand View Research的数据，预计到2025年销售额还将增加数十亿美元。但我们真的需要所有这些补充蛋白吗？这取决于情况。有优点、缺点和一些平庸之处需要考虑。

paragraphs.text: For starters, protein is critical for every cell in our body. It helps build nails, hair, bones, and muscles. It can also help you feel fuller longer than eating foods without protein. And, unlike nutrients that are found only in a few foods, protein is pretty much ubiquitous. "The typical American diet is a lot higher in protein than a lot of us think, "says registered dietitian Angela Pipitone with Johns Hopkins McKusick-Nathans Institute of Genetic Medicine. She says it's in foods many of us expect, such as beef, chicken, and other types of meat and dairy. But it's also in foods that may not come immediately to mind like vegetables, fruit, beans and grains.
paragraphs.translation: 首先，蛋白质对我们身体的每个细胞都至关重要。它有助于构建指甲、头发、骨骼和肌肉。与不含蛋白质的食物相比，它还能让你更长时间地感到饱腹。而且，与仅存在于少数食物中的营养素不同，蛋白质几乎无处不在。“典型的美式饮食中蛋白质含量比我们许多人想象的要高得多，”约翰斯·霍普金斯大学麦库西克-纳坦斯遗传医学研究所的注册营养师安吉拉·皮皮托内说。她表示，蛋白质存在于我们许多人预料的食物中，如牛肉、鸡肉和其他肉类及乳制品。但它也存在于可能不立即想到的食物中，如蔬菜、水果、豆类和谷物。

paragraphs.text: The U.S. government's recommended daily allowance (RDA) for the average adult is 50 to 60 grams of protein a day. This may sound like a lot, but Pipitone says: "We get bits of protein here and there and that really adds up throughout the day. "Take, for example, breakfast. If you ate two eggs topped with a little bit of cheese and an orange on the side, you already have 22 grams of protein. Each egg gives you 7 grams; the cheese gives you around 6 grams and the orange - about 2 grams. Add a lunch of chicken, rice, and broccoli, and you are already over the recommended 50 grams. "You can get enough protein and meet the RDA before you even get to dinner," says Pipitone.
paragraphs.translation: 美国政府推荐的普通成人每日蛋白质摄入量为50至60克。这听起来可能很多，但皮皮托内说：“我们这里一点那里一点地摄入蛋白质，全天累积起来真的很多。”以早餐为例。如果你吃两个鸡蛋，上面撒点奶酪，再配一个橙子，你已经有22克蛋白质了。每个鸡蛋提供7克；奶酪约6克；橙子约2克。加上鸡肉、米饭和西兰花的午餐，你已经超过了推荐的50克。“在晚饭之前，你就能摄入足够的蛋白质并达到推荐摄入量，”皮皮托内说。

paragraphs.text: So if it's so easy to get your protein in food, why add more in the form of powders, snack bars or a boost at your local juice bar? No need to, says Pipitone because, in fact, most of us already get enough protein in our diet. "Whole foods are always the best option rather than adding supplements," she says, noting the FDA does not regulate supplements as stringently as foods or drugs, so there could be less protein, more sugar, and some additives you wouldn't expect, such as caffeine and even steroids.
paragraphs.translation: 那么，如果从食物中获取蛋白质如此容易，为什么还要以粉末、零食棒或在当地果汁吧加蛋白的形式来增加呢？皮皮托内说没有必要，因为事实上，我们大多数人已经从饮食中摄入了足够的蛋白质。“全食物总是最佳选择，而不是添加补充剂，”她说，并指出FDA对补充剂的监管不像对食品或药品那样严格，因此可能含有更少的蛋白质、更多的糖，以及一些你意想不到的添加剂，如咖啡因甚至类固醇。

paragraphs.text: If you are considering a supplement, read the list of ingredients, she says although this is not always foolproof. "I've seen very expensive protein supplements that claim to be high quality but they might not really be beneficial for the average healthy adult," she says. "It could just be a waste of money."
paragraphs.translation: 如果你考虑使用补充剂，要阅读成分列表，她说，尽管这并不总是万无一失的。“我见过非常昂贵的蛋白质补充剂，声称高质量，但可能对普通健康成人并没有真正益处，”她说。“这可能只是浪费钱。”

paragraphs.text: But there are certain situations that do warrant extra protein. "Anytime you're in an anabolic state or building muscle," Pipitone says, such as if you're an extreme endurance athlete, training for a marathon, or you're a body builder. If you're moderately exercising for 150 minutes a week, as the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommends, or less than that, you're probably not an extreme athlete. Extreme athletes expend lots of energy breaking down and repairing and building muscles. Protein can give them the edge they need to speed along that process.
paragraphs.translation: 但在某些情况下确实需要额外蛋白质。“任何时候你处于合成代谢状态或增肌期，”皮皮托内说，比如如果你是极限耐力运动员、训练马拉松，或者你是健美运动员。如果你每周进行150分钟的中等强度运动，如疾病控制与预防中心推荐，或少于此，你可能不是极限运动员。极限运动员消耗大量能量分解、修复和构建肌肉。蛋白质可以给他们提供加速这一过程所需的优势。

paragraphs.text: Vegans can benefit from protein supplements since they do not eat animal-based protein sources like meat, dairy, or eggs. And, for someone always on-the-go who may not have time for a meal, a protein snack bar can be a good option for occasional meal replacement. Also, individuals recovering from surgery or an injury can also benefit from extra protein. So, too, can older people. At around age 60, "muscles really start to break down, " says Kathryn Starr, an aging researcher at Duke University School of Medicine," and because of that, in addition to the fact that as we get older our body's ability to break down protein is reduced, the protein needs of an older adult actually increases."
paragraphs.translation: 素食者可以从蛋白质补充剂中受益，因为他们不吃肉类、乳制品或鸡蛋等动物性蛋白来源。而且，对于总是忙碌、可能没有时间吃饭的人来说，蛋白零食棒可以是偶尔替代正餐的好选择。此外，从手术或受伤中恢复的人也可以从额外蛋白质中受益。老年人也是如此。大约在60岁左右，“肌肉开始真正分解，”杜克大学医学院的老龄化研究员凯瑟琳·斯塔尔说，“正因为如此，再加上随着年龄增长我们身体分解蛋白质的能力下降，老年人的蛋白质需求实际上增加了。”

paragraphs.text: In fact, along with her colleague Connie Bales, Starr recently conducted a small study that found that adding extra protein foods to the diet of obese older individuals who were trying to lose weight strengthened their muscles. Participants in the study were separated into two groups—one group was asked to eat 30 grams of protein per meal in the form of whole foods. That meant they were eating 90 grams of protein a day. The other group—the control group—was put on a typical low-calorie diet with about 50 to 60 grams of protein a day.
paragraphs.translation: 事实上，斯塔尔和她的同事康妮·贝尔斯最近进行了一项小型研究，发现为试图减肥的肥胖老年人饮食中添加额外蛋白质食物，可以增强他们的肌肉。研究参与者被分为两组——一组被要求每餐以全食物形式摄入30克蛋白质。这意味着他们每天摄入90克蛋白质。另一组——对照组——采用典型的低热量饮食，每天摄入约50至60克蛋白质。

paragraphs.text: After six months, researchers found the high protein group had significantly improved their muscle function - almost twice as much as the control group. "They were able to walk faster, had improved balance, and were also able to get up out of a chair faster than the control group," Starr says. All 67 participants were over 60 years of age, and both groups lost about the same amount of weight. Starr is now looking into whether high-protein diets also improve the quality of the muscle itself in seniors. She's using CT scans to measure muscle size and fat, and comparing seniors on a high-protein diet to those on regular diets. She says her findings should be available in a couple of months.
paragraphs.translation: 六个月后，研究人员发现高蛋白组的肌肉功能显著改善——几乎是对照组的两倍。“他们能够走得更快，平衡能力改善，并且也能比对照组更快地从椅子上站起来，”斯塔尔说。所有67名参与者年龄都超过60岁，两组减重幅度大致相同。斯塔尔现在正在研究高蛋白饮食是否也能改善老年人肌肉本身的质量。她使用CT扫描测量肌肉大小和脂肪，并将高蛋白饮食的老年人与常规饮食的老年人进行比较。她说她的研究结果应该在几个月内得出。

paragraphs.text: In the meantime, 70-year-old Corliss Keith, who was in the high protein group in Starr's latest study, says she feels a big difference. "I feel excellent, "she says, "I feel like I have a different body, I have more energy, I'm stronger." She says she is able to take Zumba exercise classes three times a week, work out on the treadmill and take long, brisk walks. Keith also lost more than 15 pounds. " I'm a fashionable person, so now I'm back in my three-inch heels," she says.
paragraphs.translation: 与此同时，70岁的科利斯·基思参与了斯塔尔最新研究中的高蛋白组，她表示感觉大不相同。“我感觉非常棒，”她说，“我感觉身体不一样了，我更有精力，更强壮了。”她说她每周能上三次尊巴舞课，在跑步机上锻炼，还能进行长时间的快走。基思还减掉了超过15磅。“我是个时尚的人，所以现在我又穿回三英寸高跟鞋了，”她说。

paragraphs.text: As people age, researcher Starr says muscle strength is key to helping them stay strong and continue living on their own in their own home. "I feel very much alive now," says Keith, "I feel like I could stay by myself until I'm 100."
paragraphs.translation: 随着人们年龄增长，研究员斯塔尔说，肌肉力量是帮助他们保持强壮并继续在自己家中独立生活的关键。“我现在感觉非常有活力，”基思说，“我觉得我可以独自生活到100岁。”

paragraphs.text: But can people overdo protein? Pipitone says you do have to be careful. Too much protein can cause nausea, cramps, headaches, fatigue, and bloating. Dehydration is also a risk when you eat too much protein. Pipitone says if you increase protein, you also have to increase your fluid intake. "I always tell people to make sure they're drinking enough fluids," which for the average person is 60 to 70 ounces a day, which translates into eight 8-ounce glasses of water or liquid per day.
paragraphs.translation: 但人们能过度摄入蛋白质吗？皮皮托内说你确实必须小心。过多的蛋白质可能导致恶心、抽筋、头痛、疲劳和腹胀。当你摄入过多蛋白质时，脱水也是一个风险。皮皮托内说，如果你增加蛋白质摄入，也必须增加液体摄入。“我总是告诉人们要确保摄入足够的液体，”对于普通人来说，每天是60至70盎司，相当于每天八杯8盎司的水或液体。

paragraphs.text: There have been some indications that extra protein makes the kidneys work harder which could be problematic for individuals with a history of kidney disease and for them, the supplements may increase the risk of kidney stones, she says.
paragraphs.translation: 有一些迹象表明，额外的蛋白质会使肾脏更努力工作，这对有肾脏疾病史的人来说可能有问题，对她来说，补充剂可能增加肾结石的风险，她说。

paragraphs.text: Bottom Line: if you think you need more protein in your diet, consider these questions: Are you an extreme athlete; are you recovering from injury or surgery; or are you 60 years or older? If so, adding high protein foods like eggs and meat products to your diet can be beneficial. And, if you're not sure, it is always a good idea to check with your primary care provider.
paragraphs.translation: 总结：如果你认为你的饮食需要更多蛋白质，请考虑这些问题：你是极限运动员吗；你正在从受伤或手术中恢复吗；或者你年龄在60岁或以上吗？如果是这样，在饮食中添加高蛋白食物如鸡蛋和肉类产品可能有益。而且，如果你不确定，咨询你的初级保健提供者总是一个好主意。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: Last year, a child was born at a hospital in the UK with her heart outside her body. Few babies survive this rare condition, and those who do must endure numerous operations and are likely to have complex needs. When her mother was interviewed, three weeks after her daughter's birth, she was asked if she was prepared for what might be a daunting (令人生畏的) task caring for her. She answered without hesitation that, as far as she was concerned, this would be a "privilege".
paragraphs.translation: 去年，一名儿童在英国一家医院出生，其心脏位于体外。很少有婴儿能在这种罕见状况下存活，而那些存活下来的必须经历多次手术，并可能面临复杂的需求。在她女儿出生三周后，母亲接受采访时被问及是否准备好承担照顾女儿这一可能令人生畏的任务。她毫不犹豫地回答说，在她看来，这将是一种“特权”。

paragraphs.text: Rarely has there been a better example of the power of attitude, one of our most powerful psychological tools. Our attitudes allow us to turn mistakes into opportunities, and loss into the chance for new beginnings. An attitude is a settled way of thinking, feeling and/ or behaving towards particular objects, people, events or ideologies. We use our attitudes to filter, interpret and react to the world around us. You weren't born with attitudes; rather they are all learned, and this happens in a number of ways.
paragraphs.translation: 很少有比这更好的例子来展示态度的力量，态度是我们最强大的心理工具之一。我们的态度让我们能够将错误转化为机会，将损失转化为新开始的机会。态度是一种对特定对象、人、事件或意识形态的固定的思维、感觉和/或行为方式。我们用态度来过滤、解释和回应周围的世界。你并非天生就有态度；相反，它们都是通过学习获得的，并且以多种方式发生。

paragraphs.text: The most powerful influences occur during early childhood and include both what happened to you directly, and what those around you did and said in your presence. As you acquire a distinctive identity your attitudes are further refined by the behavior of those with whom you identify—your family, those of your gender and culture, and the people you admire, even though you may not know them personally. Friendships and other important relationships become increasingly important, particularly during adolescence. About that same time and throughout adulthood, the information you receive, especially when ideas are repeated in association with goals and achievements you find attractive, also refines your attitudes.
paragraphs.translation: 最强大的影响发生在童年早期，包括直接发生在你身上的事情，以及你周围人在你面前的言行。随着你获得独特的身份，你的态度会进一步被你认同的人的行为所塑造——你的家人、与你性别和文化相同的人，以及你钦佩的人，即使你可能并不认识他们本人。友谊和其他重要关系变得越来越重要，尤其是在青春期。大约在同一时期及整个成年期，你接收的信息，特别是当想法与你认为有吸引力的目标和成就重复结合时，也会塑造你的态度。

paragraphs.text: Many people assume that our attitudes are internally consistent, that is, the way you think and feel about someone or something predicts your behavior towards them. However, many studies have found that feelings and thoughts don't necessarily predict behavior. In general, your attitudes will be internally consistent only when the behavior is easy, and when those around you hold similar beliefs. That's why, for example, many say they believe in the benefits of recycling or exercise, but don't behave in line with their views, because it takes awareness, effort and courage to go beyond merely stating that you believe something is a good idea.
paragraphs.translation: 许多人假设我们的态度是内在一致的，也就是说，你对某人或某事的想法和感觉预测了你对他们的行为。然而，许多研究发现，感觉和想法并不一定预测行为。一般来说，只有当行为容易实施，并且周围的人持有相似信念时，你的态度才会内在一致。这就是为什么，例如，许多人说他们相信回收或锻炼的好处，但行为却不符合他们的观点，因为要超越仅仅声称相信某事是好主意，需要意识、努力和勇气。

paragraphs.text: One of the most effective ways to change an attitude is to start behaving as if you already feel and think the way you'd prefer to. Take some time to reflect on your attitudes, to think about what you believe and why. Is there anything you consider a burden rather than a privilege? If so, start behaving-right now-as if the latter is the case.
paragraphs.translation: 改变态度最有效的方法之一是开始表现得好像你已经拥有你想要的感觉和想法。花些时间反思你的态度，思考你相信什么以及为什么。有什么事情你认为是负担而不是特权吗？如果是这样，现在就开始表现得好像是后者。

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。第三段提到态度受到自己认同的人的行为影响，包括'the people you admire'，对应偶像的行为。因此选项A正确。
questions.keySentence: your attitudes are further refined by the behavior of those with whom you identify—your family, those of your gender and culture, and the people you admire.

wrongOptions.B: 原文未提及教育水平对态度的影响
wrongOptions.C: 原文说同性别同文化群体的影响，并非与异性接触
wrongOptions.D: 原文强调认同人群的行为，未强调跨文化交流

questions.questionText: What do many studies find about people's feelings and thoughts?

options.label: A
options.text: They may not suggest how a person is going to behave.

options.label: B
options.text: They are in a way consistent with a person's mentality.

options.label: C
options.text: They may not find expression in interpersonal relations.

options.label: D
options.text: They are in line with a person's behavior no matter what.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。第四段指出'feelings and thoughts don't necessarily predict behavior'，即感受与想法不一定能预示行为。因此选项A正确。
questions.keySentence: many studies have found that feelings and thoughts don't necessarily predict behavior.

wrongOptions.B: 原文恰恰指出态度并不总与心理一致
wrongOptions.C: 原文未讨论是否在人际关系中表达

questions.questionText: How come many people don't do what they believe is good?

options.label: A
options.text: They can't afford the time.

options.label: B
options.text: They have no idea how to.

options.label: C
options.text: They are hypocritical.

options.label: D
options.text: They lack willpower.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。第四段指出'it takes awareness, effort and courage'才能把信念付诸行动，缺乏意志力是关键原因。因此选项D正确。
questions.keySentence: it takes awareness, effort and courage to go beyond merely stating that you believe something is a good idea.

wrongOptions.A: 原文没有提到时间不够
wrongOptions.B: 原文没有说不知道方法
wrongOptions.C: 原文未把这种行为称为虚伪

questions.questionText: What is proposed as a strategy to change attitudes?

options.label: A
options.text: Changing things that require one's immediate attention.

options.label: B
options.text: Starting to act in a way that embodies one's aspirations.

options.label: C
options.text: Adjusting one's behavior gradually over a period of time.

options.label: D
options.text: Considering ways of reducing one's psychological burdens.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。最后一段建议'start behaving as if you already feel and think the way you'd prefer to'，即按照希望具有的态度去行动。因此选项B正确。
questions.keySentence: One of the most effective ways to change an attitude is to start behaving as if you already feel and think the way you'd prefer to.

wrongOptions.A: 原文未提到优先处理急需关注的事
wrongOptions.C: 原文要求立即开始行动，并非逐步调整
wrongOptions.D: 原文不是要减少心理负担，而是把负担当作特权来对待

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: Industrial fishing for krill(磷虾) in the unspoilt waters around Antarctica is threatening the future of one of the world's last great wildernesses, according to a new report.
paragraphs.translation: 根据一份新报告，南极洲周围未受破坏水域的工业化捕捞磷虾正威胁着世界最后几大荒野之一的未来。

paragraphs.text: The study by Greenpeace analysed the movements of krill fishing vessels in the region and found they were increasingly operating "in the immediate vicinity of penguin colonies and whale-feeding grounds". It also highlights incidents of fishing boats being involved in groundings, oil spills and accidents, which posed a serious threat to the Antarctic ecosystem.
paragraphs.translation: 绿色和平组织的研究分析了该地区磷虾渔船的活动，发现它们越来越多地在“企鹅栖息地和鲸鱼觅食区的近旁”作业。报告还强调了渔船搁浅、漏油和事故的事件，这对南极生态系统构成了严重威胁。

paragraphs.text: The report, published on Tuesday, comes amid growing concern about the impact of fishing and climate change on the Antarctic. A global campaign has been launched to create a network of ocean sanctuaries to protect the seas in the region and Greenpeace is calling for an immediate halt to fishing in areas being considered for sanctuary status.
paragraphs.translation: 这份于周二发布的报告出炉之际，人们对渔业和气候变化对南极的影响日益担忧。一项全球运动已经启动，旨在建立海洋保护区网络以保护该地区的海域，绿色和平组织呼吁立即停止在可能被列为保护区地位的区域进行捕鱼。

paragraphs.text: Frida Bengtsson from Greenpeace's Protect the Antarctic campaign said: "If the krill industry wants to show it's a responsible player, then it should be voluntarily getting out of any area which is being proposed as an ocean sanctuary, and should instead be backing the protection of these huge tracts of the Antarctic."
paragraphs.translation: 绿色和平组织“保护南极”运动的Frida Bengtsson说：“如果磷虾行业想展示自己是一个负责任的参与者，那么它就应该自愿退出任何被提议为海洋保护区的区域，并转而支持保护这些南极的大片区域。”

paragraphs.text: A global campaign has been launched to turn a huge tract of Antarctic seas into ocean sanctuaries protecting wildlife and banning not just krill fishing, but all fishing. One was created in the Ross Sea in 2016, another reserve is being proposed in a vast area of the Weddell Sea, and a third sanctuary is under consideration in the area west of the Antarctic Peninsula--a key krill fishing area.
paragraphs.translation: 一项全球运动已经启动，旨在将南极海域的一大片区转变为海洋保护区，保护野生动物，并禁止不仅是磷虾捕捞，而是所有捕鱼活动。2016年在罗斯海创建了一个保护区，另一个保护区正在威德尔海的广阔区域被提议，第三个保护区正在南极半岛以西的区域考虑中——这是一个关键的磷虾捕捞区域。

paragraphs.text: The Commission for the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources(CCAMLR) manages the seas around Antarctica. It will decide on the Weddell Sea sanctuary proposal at a conference in Australia in October, although a decision on the peninsula sanctuary is not expected until later.
paragraphs.translation: 南极海洋生物资源养护委员会（CCAMLR）管理着南极洲周围的海域。它将在10月于澳大利亚举行的一次会议上决定威德尔海保护区的提案，不过关于半岛保护区的决定预计要稍后才会做出。

paragraphs.text: Keith Reid, a science manager at CCAMLR, said that the organisation sought a balance between protection, conservation and sustainable fishing in the Southern Ocean. He said although more fishing was taking place nearer penguin colonies it was often happening later in the season when these colonies were empty.
paragraphs.translation: CCAMLR的科学经理Keith Reid表示，该组织在南大洋寻求保护、养护和可持续捕鱼之间的平衡。他说，尽管捕鱼活动越来越多地靠近企鹅栖息地，但这通常发生在季节后期，当这些栖息地已经空无一物时。

paragraphs.text: "The creation of a system of marine protected areas is a key part of ongoing scientific and policy discussions in CCAMLR, " he added. "Our long-term operation in the region depends on a healthy and thriving Antarctic marine ecosystem, which is why we have always had an open dialogue with the environmental non-governmental organisations. We strongly intend to continue this dialogue, including talks with Greenpeace, to discuss improvements based on the latest scientific data. We are not the ones to decide on the establishment of marine protected areas, but we hope to contribute positively with our knowledge and experience.
paragraphs.translation: 他补充说：“建立海洋保护区体系是CCAMLR正在进行的科学和政策讨论的关键部分。我们在该地区的长期运作依赖于一个健康繁荣的南极海洋生态系统，这就是为什么我们一直与环保非政府组织进行公开对话。我们强烈希望继续这一对话，包括与绿色和平组织的会谈，以基于最新科学数据讨论改进措施。我们不是决定建立海洋保护区的机构，但我们希望用我们的知识和经验做出积极贡献。”

questionGroups.directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.questionText: What does Greenpeace's study find about krill fishing?

options.label: A
options.text: It caused a great many penguins and whales to migrate.

options.label: B
options.text: It was depriving penguins and whales of their habitats.

options.label: C
options.text: It was carried out too close to the habitats of penguins and whales.

options.label: D
options.text: It posed an unprecedented threat to the wildlife around Antarctica.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据文章第二段'The study by Greenpeace analysed the movements of krill fishing vessels in the region and found they were increasingly operating in the immediate vicinity of penguin colonies and whale-feeding grounds'，可以确定C选项'It was carried out too close to the habitats of penguins and whales.'是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'It caused a great many penguins and whales to migrate.'原文没有提到磷虾捕捞导致企鹅和鲸鱼大量迁徙。
wrongOptions.B: 'It was depriving penguins and whales of their habitats.'原文没有提到磷虾捕捞剥夺了企鹅和鲸鱼的栖息地。
wrongOptions.D: 'It posed an unprecedented threat to the wildlife around Antarctica.'虽然文章提到了对南极生态系统的威胁，但'unprecedented'一词过于绝对，原文没有使用。

questions.questionText: For what purpose has a global campaign been launched?

options.label: A
options.text: To reduce the impact of climate change on Antarctica.

options.label: B
options.text: To establish conservation areas in the Antarctic region.

options.label: C
options.text: To regulate krill fishing operations in the Antarctic seas.

options.label: D
options.text: To publicise the concern about the impact of krill fishing.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据文章第四段'A global campaign has been launched to turn a huge tract of Antarctic seas into ocean sanctuaries protecting wildlife and banning not just krill fishing, but all fishing.'，可以确定B选项'To establish conservation areas in the Antarctic region.'是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'To reduce the impact of climate change on Antarctica.'虽然文章提到了气候变化对南极的影响，但这不是全球运动的目的。
wrongOptions.C: 'To regulate krill fishing operations in the Antarctic seas.'全球运动的目的不仅仅是规范磷虾捕捞，而是建立保护区。
wrongOptions.D: 'To publicise the concern about the impact of krill fishing.'全球运动的目的不仅仅是宣传对磷虾捕捞的担忧，而是建立保护区。

questions.questionText: What is Greenpeace's recommendation to the krill industry?

options.label: A
options.text: Opting to operate away from the suggested conservation areas.

options.label: B
options.text: Volunteering to protect the endangered species in the Antarctic.

options.label: C
options.text: Refraining from krill fishing throughout the breeding season.

options.label: D
options.text: Showing its sense of responsibility by leading the global campaign.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据文章第四段'Frida Bengtsson from Greenpeace's Protect the Antarctic campaign said: If the krill industry wants to show it's a responsible player, then it should be voluntarily getting out of any area which is being proposed as an ocean sanctuary, and should instead be backing the protection of these huge tracts of the Antarctic.'，可以确定A选项'Opting to operate away from the suggested conservation areas.'是正确答案。

wrongOptions.B: 'Volunteering to protect the endangered species in the Antarctic.'虽然环保是目的之一，但原文中没有提到磷虾行业自愿保护濒危物种。
wrongOptions.C: 'Refraining from krill fishing throughout the breeding season.'原文没有提到在繁殖季节停止磷虾捕捞。
wrongOptions.D: 'Showing its sense of responsibility by leading the global campaign.'原文中没有提到磷虾行业通过领导全球运动来展示其责任感。

questions.questionText: What did CCAMLR aim to do according to its science manager?

options.label: A
options.text: Raise public awareness of the vulnerability of Antarctic species.

options.label: B
options.text: Ban all commercial fishing operations in the Southern Ocean.

options.label: C
options.text: Keep the penguin colonies from all fishing interference.

options.label: D
options.text: Sustain fishing without damaging the Antarctic ecosystem.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据文章倒数第二段'He said although more fishing was taking place nearer penguin colonies it was often happening later in the season when these colonies were empty. The creation of a system of marine protected areas is a key part of ongoing scientific and policy discussions in CCAMLR, he added. Our long-term operation in the region depends on a healthy and thriving Antarctic marine ecosystem, which is why we have always had an open dialogue with the environmental non-governmental organisations.'，可以确定D选项'Sustain fishing without damaging the Antarctic ecosystem.'是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'Raise public awareness of the vulnerability of Antarctic species.'原文没有提到提高公众对南极物种脆弱性的认识。
wrongOptions.B: 'Ban all commercial fishing operations in the Southern Ocean.'原文没有提到在南大洋禁止所有商业捕捞活动。
wrongOptions.C: 'Keep the penguin colonies from all fishing interference.'虽然文章提到了企鹅栖息地附近的捕捞活动，但没有说要完全避免干扰。

questions.questionText: How does CCAMLR define its role in the conservation of the Antarctic environment?

options.label: A
options.text: A coordinator in policy discussions.

options.label: B
options.text: An authority on big data analysis.

options.label: C
options.text: A provider of the needed expertise.

options.label: D
options.text: An initiator of marine sanctuaries.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。根据文章最后一段'Keith Reid, a science manager at CCAMLR, said that the organisation sought a balance between protection, conservation and sustainable fishing in the Southern Ocean. We are not the ones to decide on the establishment of marine protected areas, but we hope to contribute positively with our knowledge and experience.'，可以确定C选项'A provider of the needed expertise.'是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 'A coordinator in policy discussions.'虽然CCAMLR参与政策讨论，但原文没有说它是协调者。
wrongOptions.B: An authority on big data analysis.'原文没有提到CCAMLR是大数据分析的权威。
wrongOptions.D: An initiator of marine sanctuaries.'虽然CCAMLR参与海洋保护区的讨论，但原文没有说它是发起者。

questionGroups.sourceText: 牡丹花色艳丽，形象高雅，象征着和平与繁荣，因而在中国被称为"花中之王"。中国许多地方都培育和种植牡丹。千百年来，创造了许多诗歌和绘画赞美牡丹。唐代时期，牡丹在皇家园林普遍种植并被誉为国花，因而特别风行。十世纪时，洛阳古城成为牡丹栽培中心，而且这一地位一直保持到今天。现在，成千上万的国内游客蜂拥到洛阳参加一年一度的牡丹节，欣赏洛阳牡丹独特之美，同时探索九朝古都的历史。

answer.modelTranslation: Peonies, with their vibrant colors and elegant appearance, symbolize peace and prosperity, hence they are known as the 'King of Flowers' in China. Many regions in China cultivate and grow peonies. Over thousands of years, numerous poems and paintings have been created to praise the peony. During the Tang Dynasty, peonies were widely planted in royal gardens and were hailed as the national flower, making them particularly fashionable. In the tenth century, the ancient city of Luoyang became the center of peony cultivation, a status it has maintained to this day. Now, tens of thousands of domestic tourists flock to Luoyang to attend the annual Peony Festival, to appreciate the unique beauty of Luoyang peonies and to explore the history of the ancient capital of nine dynasties.
translationNotes: 注意'形象高雅'的翻译，可用elegant appearance来表达
'象征和平与繁荣'可译为symbolize peace and prosperity
'因而在中国被称为'可译为hence they are known as
'千百年来'译为over thousands of years，表示时间的跨度
'唐代时期'译为During the Tang Dynasty，注意大写首字母
'因而特别风行'可译为making them particularly fashionable
'十世纪时'译为In the tenth century，注意大写首字母和时间表达方式
'成千上万的国内游客'可译为tens of thousands of domestic tourists
'蜂拥到洛阳'可译为flock to Luoyang，注意使用动词flock表示人群聚集
scoringPoints: 准确翻译形容词和名词，如vibrant, elegant, symbolize等
恰当使用固定搭配，如King of Flowers, peace and prosperity等
时态使用恰当，描述历史和现状
词汇选择准确，如cultivate, numerous, fashionable等
句子结构完整流畅，使用合适的连接词和表达
注意专有名词和历史时期的大写，如Tang Dynasty, Luoyang等
